pre_vs_post_scale.note: Fidelity Benchmark / 2n_v3 macros snapshot END-OF-RECRUIT (pre-scaling). Firestone warbandStats are average board stats per turn; residual scaling is intended to bridge to that curve at end of recruit AFTER abstract growth.

hypothesis_revision.prior: target-gap bridge defect (residual underfills when current << pace)
hypothesis_revision.observed: At T10, residual fills most of the gap: greedy post 0.952× / Phase 2J post 0.886× Firestone, with unfilled gaps 77 / 183 on target 1601. Automated target-gap route did NOT fire. Primary automated finding: recruit_contribution_collapsed (greedy recruit Δ≈0 from T10+; Phase 2J recruit Δ negative = board sacrifice). Secondary: just_leveled 0.6× factor on universal T10 level-to-6 for greedy.
hypothesis_revision.late_game: Post-scale OVERSHOOTS Firestone T12–T14 (greedy 1.46→1.82; Phase 2J 1.19→1.55). Opposite of midgame undershoot-after-scale.
hypothesis_revision.why_2n_v3_looked_broken: 2n_v3 T9–T12 ratios (≈0.45–0.60) are pre-scale snapshots — reproduced here. They are not post-scale board strength.
hypothesis_revision.phase_2j: α=0.5 untouched. Composition-motivated board sacrifice shows as negative recruit Δ; still closer to Firestone than greedy at T12/T14 on prospective directional harm metric.

recommended_next_step_refined: Do not jump straight to a target-gap additive correction without addressing (1) whether acceptance should score post-scale vs pre-scale, and (2) recruit/effect-value contribution ≈0 after active-pool correction. If a Phase 2P scaling change is still wanted, prefer a bounded midgame correction that does not worsen T12–T14 post-scale overshoot.
